extracted.intended_audience: manufacturers, distributors, importers, retailers of cigarettes/smokeless/covered tobacco products; compliance officers; legal counsel; FDA/agency staff
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and regulatory requirements in 21 CFR Part 1140 governing the manufacture, labeling, advertising, sale, distribution, and sampling of cigarettes, smokeless tobacco, and covered tobacco products in the United States. Covers definitions, age-restriction enforcement, packaging and vending rules, advertising/labeling format limits, and prohibitions on samples, branded non-tobacco merchandise, gifts, and sponsorships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and misbranding consequence
rubrics_metrics.description: This part sets out the restrictions under the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act on the sale, distribution, and use of cigarettes, smokeless tobacco, and covered tobacco products. The failure to comply with any applicable provision in this part in the sale, distribution, and use of cigarettes, smokeless tobacco, covered tobacco products, or other tobacco products renders the product misbranded under the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Noncompliance with any provision of Part 1140 can result in the product being treated as misbranded under the FD&C Act, with whatever legal consequences flow from misbranding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose (public health objective)
rubrics_metrics.description: The purpose of this part is to establish restrictions on the sale, distribution, and use of cigarettes, smokeless tobacco, and covered tobacco products in order to reduce the number of children and adolescents who use these products, and to reduce the life‑threatening consequences associated with tobacco use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory requirements should be interpreted and applied with the stated objective of preventing youth access and use.

rubrics_metrics.name: General responsibility of manufacturers, distributors, importers, and retailers
rubrics_metrics.description: Each manufacturer, distributor, importer, and retailer is responsible for ensuring that the cigarettes, smokeless tobacco, or covered tobacco products it manufactures, labels, advertises, packages, distributes, imports, sells, or otherwise holds for sale comply with all applicable requirements under this part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entities at all points in the supply chain must affirmatively ensure compliance; passive reliance on others is insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manufacturer obligation to remove noncompliant items from points of sale
rubrics_metrics.description: Each manufacturer shall remove from each point of sale all self-service displays, advertising, labeling, and other items that the manufacturer owns that do not comply with the requirements under this part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manufacturers must proactively remove their owned materials that fail to meet Part 1140 requirements wherever they are placed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retailer responsibilities — age-based sale prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: No retailer may sell cigarettes or smokeless tobacco to any person younger than 21 years of age.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absolute prohibition on sales to under-21 persons; retailers must implement procedures to prevent such sales.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retailer responsibilities — photographic identification verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as otherwise provided, each retailer must verify by means of photographic identification containing the bearer's date of birth that no person purchasing the product is younger than 21 years of age.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ID verification is the default verification method; see exceptions (no verification required for persons over 29).

rubrics_metrics.name: ID verification exception for persons over 29
rubrics_metrics.description: No such verification is required for any person over the age of 29.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retailers may rely on apparent age >29 without photographic ID, but should be cautious about misjudgment risks and other applicable state/local laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retailer sales must be direct, face‑to‑face (no impersonal sales)
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as otherwise provided, a retailer may sell cigarettes and smokeless tobacco only in a direct, face-to-face exchange without the assistance of any electronic or mechanical device (such as a vending machine).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibited methods include vending machines and self-service displays, unless an exception applies (e.g., facility where no one under 21 is present).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sale of partial packages prohibited
rubrics_metrics.description: No retailer may break or otherwise open any cigarette or smokeless tobacco package to sell or distribute individual cigarettes or a number of unpackaged cigarettes that is smaller than the quantity in the minimum cigarette package size defined in § 1140.16(b), or any quantity of cigarette tobacco or smokeless tobacco that is smaller than the smallest package distributed by the manufacturer for individual consumer use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retailers must sell in manufacturer-intended package sizes; cannot split packs or sell smaller-than-manufacturer packages to consumers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retailer obligation to remove or bring into compliance noncompliant displays/advertising
rubrics_metrics.description: Each retailer must ensure that all self-service displays, advertising, labeling, and other items, that are located in the retailer's establishment and that do not comply with the requirements of this part, are removed or are brought into compliance with the requirements under this part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retailers must audit and correct in-store materials that violate Part 1140, not just those owned by manufacturers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Covered tobacco product-specific retailer restrictions (age, ID, vending)
rubrics_metrics.description: No retailer may sell covered tobacco products to any person younger than 21 years of age; except as otherwise provided, each retailer must verify by photographic ID containing date of birth that purchaser is not younger than 21; no such verification is required for persons over 29; a retailer may not sell covered tobacco products with the assistance of any electronic or mechanical device (such as a vending machine), except in facilities where the retailer ensures that no person younger than 21 years of age is present, or permitted to enter, at any time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parallel rules apply specifically to covered tobacco products with an explicit vending-machine/facility exception requiring strict control that minors are never present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on use of nontobacco trade/brand names
rubrics_metrics.description: A manufacturer shall not use a trade or brand name of a nontobacco product as the trade or brand name for a cigarette or smokeless tobacco product, except for a tobacco product whose trade or brand name was on both a tobacco product and a nontobacco product that were sold in the United States on January 1, 1995.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Brand-name cross-use from nontobacco products is prohibited unless longstanding (in use on both product types prior to Jan 1, 1995).

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum cigarette package size
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as otherwise provided under this section, no manufacturer, distributor, or retailer may sell or cause to be sold, or distribute or cause to be distributed, any cigarette package that contains fewer than 20 cigarettes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default minimum is 20 cigarettes per package; exceptions must be explicit in the regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on vending machines and self-service displays (general rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as otherwise provided, a retailer may sell cigarettes and smokeless tobacco only in a direct, face-to-face exchange between the retailer and the consumer. Examples of methods of sale that are not permitted include vending machines and self-service displays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule is designed to prevent anonymous/impersonal access; exceptions are narrowly carved (see mailing and adult-only facility exceptions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted impersonal sales exceptions (mail-order and secured vending)
rubrics_metrics.description: Permitted methods of sale include mail-order sales (excluding mail-order redemption of coupons and distribution of free samples through the mail) and vending machines/self-service displays that are located in facilities where the retailer ensures that no person younger than 21 years of age is present, or permitted to enter, at any time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mail-order allowed but not for coupons/free samples; vending machines/self-service allowed only in fully age‑restricted facilities with 21+ assurance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on distribution of free samples (general rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as provided, no manufacturer, distributor, or retailer may distribute or cause to be distributed any free samples of cigarettes, smokeless tobacco, or other tobacco products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General ban on free samples; narrow exception exists for smokeless tobacco in qualified adult-only facilities (subject to strict conditions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception for free samples of smokeless tobacco in qualified adult-only facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Paragraph (d)(1) does not prohibit distribution of free samples of smokeless tobacco in a qualified adult-only facility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distribution in such facilities must meet detailed facility requirements and sample-quantity limits; States/local governments may further restrict or prohibit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualified adult-only facility criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'qualified adult-only facility' means a facility or restricted area that: (A) requires each person present to provide government-issued photo ID showing at least the minimum purchase age; (B) does not sell, serve, or distribute alcohol; (C) is not located adjacent to or immediately across from a space used primarily for youth-oriented marketing/activities; (D) is a temporary structure constructed, designated, and operated as a distinct enclosed area for distributing free samples; (E) is enclosed by an opaque barrier with specified height and visibility restrictions; and (F) does not display on its exterior any tobacco product advertising, most brand names (except as area identifier), or any combination of words implying an unlawful sponsorship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The regulation prescribes detailed physical, operational, and signage constraints to reduce youth exposure and limit visibility of sampling activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample packaging and per-person limits for smokeless tobacco
rubrics_metrics.description: Samples permitted to be taken out of the qualified adult-only facility shall be limited to one package per adult consumer containing no more than 0.53 ounces (15 grams) of smokeless tobacco; if package contains individual portions, portions shall not exceed eight and total weight shall not exceed 0.53 ounces (15 grams). Manufacturers/distributors/retailers must take reasonable steps to ensure one such package per adult consumer per day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict per-person, per-day limits on sample quantity; operational controls expected to enforce limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Events and groups where free samples are prohibited even if adult-only facility
rubrics_metrics.description: Notwithstanding the qualified facility exception, no free samples of smokeless tobacco may be distributed to a sports team or entertainment group, or at any football, basketball, baseball, soccer, hockey, or other sporting/entertainment event determined by the Secretary to be covered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secretary has authority to designate covered events; distribution at many popular sporting events is specifically disallowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secretary's compliance program and reporting obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary shall implement a program to ensure compliance with the free-sample prohibition and submit a report to Congress on such compliance not later than 18 months after enactment of the Family Smoking Prevention and Tobacco Control Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative oversight and reporting are mandated to monitor enforcement of sampling restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on labels, labeling, and advertising compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: No manufacturer, distributor, or retailer may sell or distribute cigarettes or smokeless tobacco with labels, labeling, or advertising not in compliance with subpart D of this part, and other applicable requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advertising and labeling must meet subpart D specific formatting and content rules; package labels are addressed separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of permissible labeling/advertising media
rubrics_metrics.description: Advertising/labeling bearing a cigarette or smokeless tobacco brand name may be disseminated in newspapers, magazines, periodicals, billboards, posters, placards, nonpoint-of-sale promotional material (including direct mail), point-of-sale promotional material, and audio or video formats delivered at a point-of-sale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other media may be used only after notifying the agency 30 days prior (describe the medium and discuss how much it may be seen by persons younger than 18); send notice to the Office of Compliance and Enforcement, Center for Tobacco Products.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to notify FDA 30 days before using unlisted advertising mediums
rubrics_metrics.description: A manufacturer, distributor, or retailer intending to disseminate advertising/labeling in a medium not listed must notify the agency 30 days prior to use; the notice shall describe the medium and discuss the extent to which the advertising or labeling may be seen by persons younger than 18 years of age.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification must be sent to the specified FDA office/address; provides FDA opportunity to evaluate youth exposure risk for novel media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subpart D does not apply to package labels
rubrics_metrics.description: This subpart D does not apply to cigarette or smokeless tobacco package labels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Package labels are regulated elsewhere; advertising/labeling rules in subpart D apply to other forms of promotion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format and content requirement — black text on white background
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as provided, each manufacturer, distributor, and retailer advertising or causing to be advertised any labeling or advertising for cigarettes or smokeless tobacco shall use only black text on a white background.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a stringent formatting rule intended to limit graphical/attention-getting content; limited exceptions apply for in-facility advertising and adult publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception for in‑facility advertising where vending/self-service allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: Advertising in any facility where vending machines and self-service displays are permitted is allowed provided that the advertising is not visible from outside the facility and that it is affixed to a wall or fixture in the facility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In-facility ads must be contained and non-visible from outside to reduce youth exposure; still subject to black-text-on-white requirement unless otherwise exempted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception for adult publications and definition thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Advertising appearing in any publication that the manufacturer demonstrates is an 'adult publication' is exempt from the black text on white requirement; an adult publication is one whose readers younger than 18 constitute 15% or less of total readership as measured by competent and reliable survey evidence, and that is read by fewer than 2 million persons younger than 18 as measured by competent and reliable survey evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Burden on advertiser to demonstrate publication meets both numeric thresholds with reliable survey evidence; two-prong test to qualify as adult.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audio and video format limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Audio format shall be limited to words only with no music or sound effects. Video formats shall be limited to static black text only on a white background. Any audio with the video shall be limited to words only with no music or sound effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict content limits for AV formats delivered at point-of-sale to avoid use of music/sound and dynamic visuals that could appeal to youth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on marketing/licensing/distribution of non-tobacco items bearing tobacco brand indicia
rubrics_metrics.description: No manufacturer or distributor of imported cigarettes or smokeless tobacco may market, license, distribute, sell, or cause to be marketed, licensed, distributed, or sold any item (other than cigarettes or smokeless tobacco or roll-your-own paper) or service which bears the brand name, logo, symbol, motto, selling message, recognizable color or pattern of colors, or any other indicia of product identification identical or similar to those used for any brand of cigarettes or smokeless tobacco.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents brand extension and branded merchandising that could promote tobacco to youth via non-tobacco items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ban on gifts or items given in consideration of tobacco purchase or proofs-of-purchase
rubrics_metrics.description: No manufacturer, distributor, or retailer may offer or cause to be offered any gift or item (other than cigarettes or smokeless tobacco) to any person purchasing cigarettes or smokeless tobacco in consideration of the purchase thereof, or to any person in consideration of furnishing evidence, such as credits, proofs-of-purchase, or coupons, of such a purchase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibits promotional giveaways or loyalty incentives tied to tobacco purchases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on sponsoring events in brand-identifying marks (sponsorship ban)
rubrics_metrics.description: No manufacturer, distributor, or retailer may sponsor or cause to be sponsored any athletic, musical, artistic, or other social or cultural event, or any entry or team in any event, in the brand name, logo, symbol, motto, selling message, recognizable color or pattern of colors, or other indicia of product identification identical or similar to those used for any tobacco brand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sponsorship in tobacco brand indicia is banned; limited exception allows corporate-name sponsorship if the corporate name (without any brand indicia) was registered and in use in the U.S. prior to January 1, 1995, and does not include any brand name.
